channel.title: SeatScope — guides
channel.description: Search every institute in the official CSAB 2026 release, see the published opening ranks for each branch, and check a seat against real round-to-round movement — with the sample size and the uncertainty stated, never a made-up percentage.

item.title: Home state, other state, all India: which quota your rank is competing in
item.description: NITs split most seats into home-state and other-state quotas. Which one you are in changes the number you should be reading — often by thousands of ranks.

item.title: Float, freeze or surrender: the decision, without the folklore
item.description: What each option actually does to the seat you are holding, what it risks, and the three questions that settle the choice faster than any advice thread.

item.title: What rank drift is, and why it beats last year's cutoff
item.description: Drift is how far a seat's closing rank moves between counselling rounds. It is measurable, it is directional, and it is a better guide than a single…

item.title: Opening rank vs closing rank: what each one can actually prove
item.description: An opening rank is one-sided evidence. It can prove a seat was within reach and it can never prove one was out of reach. Here is why, and how to use it…
